segments.text: American Fork City Council — Budget Workshop — February 19–20, 2026:

entities.speaker: David H. Bunker
entities.remark-context: Police/courts construction and police staffing priorities

segments.text: During the city’s strategic review, City Administrator David Bunker reported that design of the police/courts project was complete and the construction work had gone out to bid. The workshop’s resulting high-priority list also included police and fire staffing needs.

entities.label: Police/courts construction and police staffing priorities

segments.text: The workshop recorded an important facility milestone—the police/courts project had moved from design to bidding—and retained police staffing among the city’s high-priority needs. The cited expenditure figure covers police and fire together and should not be read as a police-only percentage.
Relevant passages from the official meeting minutes:

Police and Courts. The design has been completed, and the bid has been out for construction.

Ms. Montoy went over the expenditures. Personnel was the largest expense in the general fund; however, citywide the largest was capital expenditures. She went over the expenditures by department, pointing out public safety was approximately 54% of the expenditures. She compared the general fund expenditures according to type. Personnel increased, but operations and transfers decreased. The expenditure increase was about 1.5%.

The high priority items included:
• Staffing Needs – fire and police personnel.
